title: Japan Campervan — Honshu & Hokkaido
subtitle: 雪・車・山 — snow, van, mountains · two legs, six resorts, one van
coverCredit: Mt Yotei from the Niseko slopes
summary: The deepest, driest powder on Earth, chased in a campervan — no fixed plan, no lift queues, just a van and the snow forecast. Two legs: a **Honshu warm-up** (Hakuba → Nozawa Onsen → Yuzawa) in the van, then a quick flight to **Hokkaido** for the big one (Niseko/Rusutsu/Kiroro → Furano → Asahidake). The spine is fixed; the daily stops are decided by the storm. Two missions make the trip: **climbing Mt Yotei** and the **Asahidake volcanic bowls**.

features.title: The best snow on Earth, minus the crowds
features.description: Hokkaido's annual snowfall is measured in **metres, not centimetres** — Niseko averages 15 m, Kiroro is Japan's snowiest resort at 21 m. And January is the heart of it. The van is the move: you sleep at the resort car park and wake up first in line, chase the storm from one valley to the next, and never pay hotel prices. The honest bit: van nights are cold (we'll have a proper heater), there's no toilet on board (Japan's onsens and service stations are legendary), and we sleep at ski-resort car parks and onsen towns — exactly how the locals do it.

features.title: One spine, two missions, ten wildcards
features.description: Roughly **600 km** over 10–12 days. The spine is fixed; the daily stops are decided by the **snow forecast** — that's the whole point of the van. Honshu first (Hakuba → Nozawa Onsen → Yuzawa: three of the best resorts on the main island), then fly to Hokkaido for the deep stuff. Everything else is a wildcard to decide on the road.

features.title: Yotei & Asahidake — the reason we go
features.description:
Two full alpine days that no lift ticket can buy.

**Mt Yotei** — "Hokkaido's Fuji", 1,898 m, a perfect stratovolcano. We climb it on our own skin track from the Annupuri side: a full day, wind-loaded faces, and a summit view over the whole volcano. Check conditions, pick the weather window.

**Asahidake** — ropeway to 1,600 m on Hokkaido's highest peak, in the Daisetsuzan range. Volcanic bowls and steaming vents, terrain you can't get anywhere else. Both need a splitboard/skins and avalanche gear.

practical.notes: **Driving**: left-hand traffic, winter tyres mandatory, 4WD + heater essential in the van. **Onsen etiquette**: wash before you soak, no swimwear, tattoos may need covering (ask for private baths). **Food**: konbini breakfasts, ramen lunches, hotpot dinners — budget ~¥3,000–5,000/day pp. **Weather windows**: January storms come in pulses — some days we ride lifts, some we earn turns, some we eat ramen and wait for the next one. That's the adventure.

days.title: Fly to Tokyo → pick up the van
days.notes: Day 1 of 10. Land NRT/HND, first bowl of ramen, pick up the campervan (4WD, winter tyres, heater). Drive towards the mountains.

blocks.title: BRU → Tokyo
blocks.description: Direct or one stop — land afternoon. Roughly €1,000–1,200 return via Sapporo.

blocks.title: Campervan #1 pickup
blocks.description: Honshu van, 4–5 days. Japan Camper or Samurai — make sure it has a heater and 4WD.

blocks.title: First ramen
blocks.description: Tokyo ritual before the mountains. Ippudo or a hole-in-the-wall in Shinjuku.

days.title: Hakuba — Happo One
days.notes: First turns on Honshu. Happo One is the classic — big alpine terrain, and the 1998 Olympic venue. Legs will be fresh.

blocks.title: Happo One full day
blocks.description: Alpine bowls off the gondola; if the weather window is open, the traverse to Hakuba Goryu or Tsugaike is on.

blocks.title: Decide
blocks.description: Hakuba for 2 days or push on? Happo One → Nozawa is ~2h drive.

days.title: Nozawa Onsen
days.notes: One of Japan's last true ski villages: narrow streets, 13 public baths, and a proper mountain above it. Powder stashes under the Yamabiko chair.

blocks.title: Nozawa Onsen full day
blocks.description: Yamabiko, Karasawa, and the legendary tree runs. Village onsen after — the whole point of staying here.

blocks.title: Onsen crawl
blocks.description: 13 public baths, 3 of them free. Wash before you soak — and no swimwear.

days.title: Yuzawa — Kagura & Naeba
days.notes: Yuzawa is the snowiest side of the main island — Kagura and Naeba catch the Japan Sea storms. Open day: if the forecast is pumping, stay another day.

blocks.title: Kagura or Naeba
blocks.description: Kagura: higher, steeper, less crowded. Naeba: the classic. Both under the same ticket.

items.label: Chase Honshu storm vs fly to Hokkaido a day early

days.title: Open day — storm chase or fly early
days.notes: Wildcard day. Options: (a) one more Honshu powder day if the storm is here, (b) drive back, drop the van, fly Tokyo → New Chitose this evening and gain a full Hokkaido day. Decide by breakfast.

blocks.title: Things to decide
blocks.description: Hokkaido van pickup at New Chitose, first onsen night, and where the first storm day goes: Niseko or Kiroro.

blocks.title: Tokyo → New Chitose
blocks.description: ~1h40 flight. Book flexible; the Hokkaido van pickup is at the airport.

days.title: Hokkaido — Niseko base
days.notes: This is why we came. Grand Hirafu first — the classic. If the storm is dumping on Kiroro instead, chase it. The van means we can.

blocks.title: Grand Hirafu
blocks.description: The most famous powder resort on Earth for a reason. Sidecountry gates off the top, Hanazono trees if it's deep.

blocks.title: First Hokkaido onsen + kaisen-don
blocks.description: Kutchan or Hirafu — seafood bowl and a soak after day one.

days.title: Rusutsu & Kiroro — wherever the storm hits
days.notes: Open day. Rusutsu: empty glades and a resort that feels like a theme park. Kiroro: Japan's snowiest resort, 21 m a year. Both ~1h from Hirafu. Storm map decides.

blocks.title: Rusutsu
blocks.description: Isola and East mountains, glades for days, almost no queues.

blocks.title: Kiroro
blocks.description: 21 m of annual snowfall — the deepest resort in Japan. Peak-side trees when it's nuking.

days.title: Mt Yotei mission
days.notes: The reason we came. Skin up Hokkaido's Fuji (1,898 m) from the Annupuri side — full alpine day, our own track, summit view over the whole volcano. Pick the weather window: needs a clear day. Splitboard + avalanche gear.

blocks.title: Yotei skin track
blocks.description: Start at Annupuri base early. 6–8h round trip, wind-loaded faces on the way down. Check the forecast — this is a weather-window day.

days.title: Furano → Asahidake
days.notes: Inland to drier, colder powder. Furano: wide-open runs and far fewer people (Mt Racey on the way for extra dumps). Then Asahidake — ropeway to 1,600 m on Hokkaido's highest peak, volcanic bowls and steaming vents.

blocks.title: Furano
blocks.description: Central belt: drier snow, best when Niseko is tracked out.

blocks.title: Asahidake bowls
blocks.description: Ropeway to 1,600 m, then it's all you. Volcanic vents steam through the snow. Backcountry — beacon, probe, shovel.

days.title: Flex morning → fly home
days.notes: Wildcard morning: one last run at whichever resort has the most snow, return the van at New Chitose, fly home. Ten days, two missions, ten wildcards — see you at the next one.

blocks.title: Wrap up
blocks.description: Return van clean-ish, dump gear, grab last onigiri at the konbini. Debrief on the plane: which storm day wins?

blocks.title: New Chitose → Brussels
blocks.description: Return flight via Tokyo or direct seasonal. ~€1,000–1,200 total.
